column4: The Holy Spirit is not a new spirit but is of God and has been with God since the very beginning. In Genesis 1:2 the Spirit of God is hovering on the waters during creation. In Nehemiah 9:20, the scriptures say that it was the Spirit who instructed the people in the wilderness. It was by this same Holy Spirit that God anointed the kings, judges, and prophets in the Old Testament. In Joel 2:28-29 the Spirit is promised to be poured out on all mankind. It was by this same Holy Spirit that God raised Jesus from the dead, and now dwells in us (Romans 8:11). There is only one Holy Spirit, and He has always been the same. How He works with people has looked different at different times, but His heart has never changed.
column5: The Holy Spirit is not a newly arisen spirit, but is from God and has been with God from the very beginning. In Genesis 1:2, the Spirit of God was moving over the waters at creation. In Nehemiah 9:20, the Word says that it was this Spirit who taught the people in the wilderness. It was by this same Holy Spirit that God anointed kings, judges, and prophets in the Old Testament. In Joel 2:28–29 it is promised that the Spirit will be poured out on all flesh. It was by this same Holy Spirit that God raised Jesus from the dead, and He now dwells in us (Romans 8:11). There is only one Holy Spirit, and He has always been the same. The way He has worked with people has seemed different at various times, but His heart has never changed.

This was when they received the Holy Spirit within them, allowing them to abide and commune with God. This will be discussed at greater depth later in this chapter as well as the chapters on sanctification and baptism.

column4: The Holy Spirit is first and foremost, from and of God. The scriptures refer to the Spirit as the Spirit of God, or the Spirit of the Lord, or the Spirit of Christ, while these highlight different aspects, they are all one in the same. The Holy Spirit, being fully God, is also eternal and is holy (blameless, innocent, pure, not profane). Some translations refer to the Holy Spirit as the Holy Ghost.
column5: The Holy Spirit, first and foremost, is from God and belongs to God. The Scriptures refer to the Spirit with titles such as the Spirit of God, or the Spirit of the Lord, or the Spirit of Christ; although these titles highlight different aspects, they are all one and the same. The Holy Spirit, being fully God, is also eternal and holy (without blemish, without sin, pure, not impure). In some translations the Holy Spirit is also called the “Holy Ghost.”

column4: The word spirit in Greek is **Pneuma** (**NYOO-mah** - **G4151**), it means breath, or wind. The Hebrew word for spirit means the same. Breath is significant as we need it in constant supply to live. It was God's breath that He blew into Adam to bring Him to life, likewise it was Jesus' breath that He breathed last before He died on the cross. Without breath there is no life. Breath like wind can be felt and experienced but are not as easily observed as other ‘elements’ water, fire, earth.
column5: The word for spirit in Greek is **Pneuma** (**NYOO-mah** - **G4151**); meaning breath, or wind. The Hebrew word for spirit has the same meaning. Breath matters because we continually need it to live. It was the breath of God that was breathed into Adam to make him alive; likewise it was the breath of Jesus that he exhaled for the last time before he died on the cross. Without breath there is no life. Breath, like wind, can be felt and experienced but is not as easily seen as the other ‘elements’ of water, fire, earth.

column4: Diving deeper, the Spirit brings conviction of these three truths:
column5: Looking more deeply, the Spirit convicts with respect to these three truths:

column4: 1.  **Conviction of sin**: Revealing the reality of human rebellion against God, drawing men’s attention to the depravity of their own lives.
column5: 1.  **Conviction regarding sin**: revealing the reality of humanity’s rebellion against God and drawing people's attention to the ruin of their own lives.

column4: 2.  **Conviction of righteousness**: Demonstrating Jesus’ perfect fulfillment of the Father’s will, and that Jesus' sacrifice provided the one-time atonement needed for forgiveness of sins.
column5: 2.  **Conviction regarding righteousness**: showing Jesus’ complete fulfillment of the Father’s will, and that Jesus’ sacrifice provided the once-for-all atonement necessary for the forgiveness of sins.

column4: 3.  **Conviction of judgment**: Affirming the defeat of Satan, the certainty of God’s justice, and that all will stand a judgement for their life's work and deeds.
column5: 3.  **Conviction regarding judgment**: affirming the defeat of Satan, the certainty of God’s justice, and that all will stand before judgment for the deeds and acts of their lives.

column4: The Holy Spirit brings supernatural boldness to proclaim the witness of the Gospel in the face of persecution. The outcome of this empowerment can be described, but it's best experienced. People are healed physically and emotionally, the dead raised, those tormented by evil spirits are set free, people with hard hearts turn and repent.

column4: ## Building a Relationship with the Holy Spirit
column5: ## Establishing a Relationship with the Holy Spirit

column4: Every relationship takes time and experience to develop deeply. The Holy Spirit is our advocate, our comforter, our helper, and our guide. He empowers us and sanctifies us.
column5: Every relationship takes time and experience to deepen. The Holy Spirit is our Advocate, our Comforter, our Helper, and our Guide. He empowers us and sanctifies us.

column4: Start to think of the Holy Spirit as you would a person. In our relationship we can both work to build it or do things that weaken our relationship. He can be ignored, He can be quenched, He can be blasphemed, or He can be listened to, honored, and obeyed.
column5: Start by considering the Holy Spirit as a person. In our relationship we can both work to build it and do things that weaken it. He can be ignored, he can be quenched, he can be blasphemed, or he can be listened to, honored, and obeyed.

column4: Don’t ignore the voice of the Holy Spirit. He is always speaking to us and the church. If you don’t yet know how to distinguish the voice of the Holy Spirit, it takes time, willingness, and effort (like all healthy and beneficial relationships). But don’t worry, you already have built into you all the necessary parts needed to start to develop a personal relationship with the Holy Spirit.
column5: Do not ignore the voice of the Holy Spirit. He is always speaking to us and to the Church. If you still don’t know how to discern the voice of the Holy Spirit, it takes time, willingness, and effort (like all healthy and beneficial relationships). But don’t worry, everything necessary to begin cultivating a personal relationship with the Holy Spirit has already been placed within you.

column4: The quickest and most reliable ways to build an effective relationship with the Holy Spirit is to
column5: The quickest and most reliable ways to build an effective relationship with the Holy Spirit are to

column4: 1.  Call out to Him **individually** in prayer, pause and wait for Him to speak.
column5: 1.  In prayer, call on Him **individually**, pause, and wait for Him to speak.

column4: 2.  Call out to Him as part of a **group** of people who know Him (the church), pause, and wait for Him to speak.
column5: 2.  As part of a **group** of people who know Him (the Church), call on Him, pause, and wait for Him to speak.

column4: I use the phrase ‘call out’ to mean literally, with your mouth, or however you speak (with your hands if you cannot speak aloud with your mouth). Why speak? A few reasons:
column5: I use the phrase ‘call on’ in its literal sense: with your mouth, or however you speak (with your hands if you cannot speak aloud with your mouth). Why speak? A few reasons:

column4: 1.  We are speaking spirits made in God's image. God speaks, and so do we.
column5: 1.  We are speaking spirits made in the image of God. God speaks, and so do we.

column4: 2.  We use speaking as the primary way to communicate. You can also write down what you want to say (journaling) and speak it aloud.
column5: 2.  We use speech as the primary way of communication. You can also write what you want to say (journaling) and speak it out loud.

column4: 3.  Speaking is an intentional act, and indicates to the party you are talking to, that you’d like to engage them in a conversation.
column5: 3.  Speaking is a deliberate act and shows the one you are talking to that you are willing to engage them in conversation.

column4: #### What should you say?
column5: #### What should you say?

column4: If you’ve never talked to God, try introducing yourself. Sure, it will feel a bit weird, but that discomfort is okay and temporary. Along with introducing yourself, tell God that you want to talk to Him and that you want Him to talk back to you.
column5: If you have never spoken with God, try introducing yourself. It will, of course, feel a bit strange, but that discomfort is okay and temporary. Along with introducing yourself, tell God that you want to talk with Him and that you want Him to talk with you.

column4: Consider asking Him a question. It doesn’t have to be a deep theological question; it can start simple. Can you show me Your love for me? Why do I have a certain feeling? What would You like to tell me?
column5: Consider asking Him a question. It doesn’t have to be a deep theological question; it can start simple. Can you show me your love for me? Why do I feel a certain way? What would you like to say to me?

column4: #### Then what?
column5: #### So what next?

column4: Well in all effective relationships you speak for a bit, then you pause and listen. God will speak.
column5: Well, in all effective relationships, you talk a bit, then you pause and listen. God will speak.

column4: God speaks in many ways, but He wants to do it personally, and internally. It will likely not be an audible voice (like if your best friend was to say your name aloud) but it will be an internal voice that speaks to your heart and mind. Elijah refers to this as the ‘still small voice’ (1 Kings 19:11-13).
column5: God speaks in many ways, but He wants to do so in a personal and inward way. It likely will not be an audible voice (like when your best friend says your name out loud) but an inner voice that speaks to your heart and mind. Elijah refers to this as the ‘still small voice’ (1 Kings 19:11-13).

column4: The most common ways that I've personally witnessed God talk to people, and I've been blessed to help dozens of people learn how to talk to God directly, is some combination of the following:
column5: The most common ways I have personally seen God speak to people—and I have had the privilege of helping dozens learn how to speak directly with God—are a combination of the following:

column4: - A knowing - the person talking to God gets an immediate understanding that helps them.
column5: - An awareness - the person who is talking with God immediately receives an impression that helps them.

column4: - A picture - also known in the scriptures as a vision or a dream (a vision is when you are awake, a dream is when you are asleep), God will give you a picture in your mind. Perhaps it’s a memory, or place you’ve been or know? Explore the picture, what do you see? What do you feel as a result? What’s happening?
column5: - An image - which in the Scriptures is also known as a vision or a dream (a vision is when you are awake, a dream is when you are asleep), God places an image in your mind. It might be a memory, or a place you have been or know. Examine the image: what do you see? As a result, how do you feel? What is happening?

column4: - An inner voice - like an audible voice, but one that only you can hear, and spoken into your heart and mind.
column5: - An inner voice - like an audible voice, but one that only you yourself hear and that speaks in your heart and mind.

column4: #### What will God say?
column5: #### What will God say?

column4: Not sure! But that’s the fun in it. I can say that He is NOT the spirit of fear, but of perfect love and that it will never violate the teaching of the scriptures. E.g., God will never tell you to commit an extra-marital affair.
column5: I'm not sure! But that's the beauty of it. I can say that He is not a spirit of fear, but the Spirit of perfect love, and He will never violate the teachings of Scripture. For example, God will never tell you to engage in an extramarital relationship.

column4: Now what?
column5: So what should we do now?

column4: Keep the dialogue going! It’s really that simple.
column5: Keep the conversation going! It really is that simple.

column4: ### Why build a relationship?
column5: ### Why build a relationship?

column4: The Holy Spirit is the Helper. The Helper helps us! The work goes much more smoothly if we have a shared language, and relationship with Him. Can you imagine trying to work with someone in your job if you had no relationship, did not speak the same language, and couldn't communicate?!
column5: The Holy Spirit is the Helper. A helper helps us! Things go much more smoothly if we have a common language and a relationship with Him. Can you imagine trying to work with someone at your job when you have no relationship, don't speak the same language, and can't communicate?!

column4: We serve a God who wants to communicate with us. Jesus said that His sheep know His voice (John 10:27), we have built into us all already the natural abilities we need, but we may lack experienced proficiency.
column5: We serve a God who wants to communicate with us. Jesus said that His sheep know His voice (John 10:27), we all already have the natural abilities needed within us, but we may lack the skill that comes from experience.

column4: Speaking from personal experience, a personal and active relationship with the Holy Spirit is one of the best things about being a Christian. His presence brings us peace, comfort, and direction, but only if you know how to seek, listen, and obey Him.
column5: From personal experience, having a personal and active relationship with the Holy Spirit is one of the best aspects of being a Christian. His presence brings us peace, comfort, and guidance, but only if you know how to seek Him, listen, and obey.

column4: Develop a sensitivity with the Holy Spirit. Like many married people over time, you can communicate with your spouse in a unique way and sometimes just through a look. The look alone tells you everything you need to know about what just happened and what's going to happen. Build that type of sensitivity and familiarity with the Holy Spirit. Include Him in your whole life, this is a wonderful part of your relationship with Him that will provide so much depth and richness to your walk of faith.
column5: Cultivate a sensitivity to the Holy Spirit within yourself. Like many married couples, over time you can communicate with your spouse in a unique way, and sometimes with just a look. That look alone tells you everything you need to know about what has happened and what is going to happen. Build that same kind of sensitivity and familiarity with the Holy Spirit. Involve Him in your whole life; this is a wonderful part of your relationship with Him that will add great depth and richness to your walk of faith.

column4: The Holy Spirit has come to lead us and guide us, to empower us to be God’s people, and to see the people of the Earth radically transformed, delivered from the kingdom of darkness into the kingdom of light. Getting to know him, building trust with Him is essential to everyday life and to accomplish the work that Jesus has for us to do.
column5: The Holy Spirit has come to lead and guide us, to empower us to be the people of God, and to see the people of the earth fundamentally transformed, delivered from the kingdom of darkness and transferred into the kingdom of light. Knowing Him and building trust with Him is essential for daily life and for accomplishing what Jesus has appointed for us.
